title: As the Singhs stood on the river bank after beating a retreat,

blocks.text: As the Singhs stood on the river bank after beating a retreat, they found the river flowing in full torrent and flood. Whirlpools churned across the current, uprooted trees came hurtling downstream, and even great stones and boulders were being dragged away by the force of the water.

The Khalsa called for someone to test the passage so the rest might follow, and two brothers from Dalewal entered the current to sound a crossing. They never returned, and their loss convinced the camp that the river offered no real escape from the tightening Mughal pursuit.

After that failed attempt, the Singhs concluded that an open death in battle was better than drowning helplessly in the torrent. Remembering the Guru's praise for one who dies fighting facing the enemy, they abandoned thoughts of a crossing and prepared to meet their attackers on land.
